newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: FORECAST-Nomura sees slowdown in Slovak GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Nomura sees slowdown in Slovak GDP growth.

text.p: Nomura International has forecast Slovak real gross domestic product (GDP) to grow six percent for whole of 1996 and slow to five percent growth in 1997, according to a research report obtained on Monday.

In its East European economic quarterly Nomura Research Institute forecast that Slovakia's current account deficit would total $1.1 billion, or 5.8 percent of GDP, by the end of 1996, increasing to $1.5 billion, 7.0 percent of GDP in 1997.
Slovak GDP grew 7.1 percent in the first half this year, up from 6.1 percent for the January-June period last year, boosted mainly by domestic consumption.
Real GDP rose 7.4 percent for the whole of 1995.
The Slovak government earlier this year forecast the GDP to grow 6.0-6.2 percent in the 1996-1997 period.

It said the higher current account deficit of $737 million in the first half this year -- up from $379 million for the first six months of 1995 -- was caused by a strong increase in domestic demand, an insufficient flexibility of the economy to react to the demand increase, and a static exchange rate.
The Slovak current account recorded a deficit for the January-August period of $957.3 million, compared with a $607.7 surplus over the same period last year.
Nomura said Slovakia, like its former federation partner Czech Republic, had shown indications of an overheated economy.

It said the response to this fact, the tightening of the monetary policy, had been both later and more timid in Slovakia than in the Czech Republic, where it had been applied since the last quarter of 1994.
Nomura said the tightening of monetary policy in Slovakia would have to be much more decisive in order to increase the banks' costs of funding inducing them to raise lending rates.
